analyst_view.overall: Early view: Sassuolo sacked Aquilani after five straight defeats, and multiple reports say Roberto D'Aversa is taking over, though that was not official when this was written; this would be his first game. Genoa lost 2-1 to Milan but out-shot them 17-6, after three straight wins, and De Rossi had an almost full squad. Both sides are near the bottom, so the result matters to both.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals. Sassuolo's games have been the highest-scoring in Serie A at over four a game, but a new coach usually starts by making his side harder to beat, and Genoa's games average only about 2.5 goals. Those pull in opposite directions, so I stay with the number.

corners.text: The site expects 8.9 corners. I lean lower: Sassuolo's home games have averaged under eight corners and Genoa's away games about 7.4. Neither side builds its attack around crosses and set pieces.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards. I lean slightly higher: both sides' games have averaged a little over four cards at these venues, and this is a nervy game near the bottom with a new coach demanding effort. Genoa collected two more bookings against Milan, and Sassuolo had a red card at home to Lazio last month.

shots.text: The site expects 24.7 shots, close to what both teams produce: Sassuolo's home games have averaged about 25 shots and Genoa's away games about 24. Genoa did take 17 shots against Milan, so a small move up is possible, but not enough to lean.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.3 shots on target. I lean slightly higher because Sassuolo allow 6.8 on target a game, the most in the league, and their home games have averaged over ten. Genoa's own accuracy is poor, so the lean is small.
